     5	## Concept
     6	
     7	<!-- Written by the Team before the code: your own choice, a few sentences per answer. Everything else in the Submission follows from it. -->
     8	
     9	**Enterprise:** A 3D digital twin of an open-pit mine's loading, haulage, road and primary-crusher system.
    10	
    11	**Users:** The mine dispatcher and shift supervisor.
    12	
    13	**Decision:** It helps them decide how to keep ore moving safely and steadily when a truck breaks down, a haul road closes, or crusher capacity falls. The operator compares throughput, queue, cycle-time and utilization effects before choosing a response.
    14	
    15	**Why this choice:** Haulage connects several mine facilities, so its problems and consequences are understandable in a live 3D view. Moving equipment, queues, rerouting and crusher flow also make a strong demonstration of connected twins rather than a decorative dashboard.
    16	
    17	**Real or fictional:** The displayed mine is a fictional, reduced demonstration layout calibrated from the anonymized North Pit Mine configuration published by the MIT-licensed OpenMines project. Synthetic live telemetry is clearly distinguished from the sourced reference parameters.

The road restriction lengthens travel, eliminating the loading queue while trucks remain continuously busy and the crusher becomes underfed.     88	## Data and Assumptions
    89	
    90	Live telemetry is synthetic and deterministic. It is not presented as measurements from an operating mine.
    91	
    92	The inspectable Data and Asset Layer is indexed in `ademix/data/README.md`. Its fleet specification, telemetry dictionary, and 3D model manifest distinguish sourced references, team assumptions, derived metrics, synthetic telemetry, and bundled assets.
    93	
    94	The main calibration source is OpenMines' anonymized `north_pit_mine.json`, included at `ademix/data/openmines/north_pit_mine.json` with its MIT license. The submitted reduced model uses its 77 t truck capacity, 25 km/h travel speed, approximately 20.32 t shovel pass, 1.5 minute shovel cycle, one minute dump duration, and route-distance scale. Four shovel passes give a rounded six-minute loading duration for the 77 t truck. Team Ademix deliberately uses six trucks instead of the full source fleet so the state is understandable and the 3D scene remains usable under software rendering.
    95	
    96	The displayed route geometry and terraced pit are fictional and simplified. The rated crusher capacity is an explicit 900 t/h planning assumption, not an equipment-manufacturer claim. With one six-minute loading resource, the modeled baseline supply is 770 t/h. Projected steady-state throughput is constrained by the minimum of fleet supply, loader supply, and crusher capacity. Five healthy trucks can still saturate the loader after one truck fails, so the breakdown's long-run analytical limit remains 770 t/h; its location-dependent transient is material, with the documented returning-lane first-hour reference falling from 770.0 to 691.0 t/h when triggered after the common four-hour warm-up. Restricted-road operation projects approximately 647.3 t/h and crusher slowdown 495 t/h. Actual processed ore remains mass-conserving: unprocessed deliveries accumulate in the ROM inventory, so observed cumulative throughput takes time to converge after a scenario change.
    97	
    98	Exact provenance, checksum, license, modifications, and rejected asset sources are recorded in `DATA_LICENSES.md` and `REUSE_CATALOG.md`. No confidential or personal operational data is used.
    99	
   100	## Mine visualization
   101	
   102	Open <http://localhost:4173> after following `README.md`. The command center shows a terraced pit, haul route, loading face, primary crusher, stockpile, and six production trucks. Production-truck state, payload, route progress, KPIs and scenario comparison come from Eclipse Ditto; paint schemes are fixed identifiers. Left-drag pans, right-drag rotates, the wheel zooms toward the pointer, and double-click inspects equipment. Software rendering automatically selects Light graphics; the Graphics button switches between Light and Balanced. Models and soil textures are bundled locally. The authoritative Layer 1 scene is the default route; `?stage=ingestion` is retained as an equivalent explicit inspection URL.
   103	
   104	## Limitations
   105	
   106	- This is a decision-demonstration model, not an engineering design, safety system, or production forecast.
   107	- Route traffic is simplified; trucks do not yet model passing, intersections, grade-dependent rimpull, or dispatch to multiple faces.
   108	- The enlarged ten-turn visual route is not a surveyed 3.2 km alignment. Progress maps to the simulated route; visual scale/grade and timing are not a validated engineering model.
   109	- Two waste trucks and surrounding support facilities are visual context, not additional operational twins or scored simulation modules. Road restriction slows traffic; alternate-route dispatch is not implemented.
   110	- Only one operating condition is active at a time, allowing a clear controlled comparison and reliable reset.
   111	- Fuel percentage is a synthetic visualization signal and is not calibrated to a specific engine or duty cycle.
   112	- Scenario projections use a simplified steady-state cycle calculation; observed cumulative throughput takes simulated time to converge after a scenario change.
   113	- The current procedural low-poly mine prioritizes reliable software rendering. Any third-party visual asset will be included only after exact license and performance verification.
   114	
   115	## Presentation
   116	
   117	`presentation.pdf` in the repository root uses current C5 interface evidence, current model counts and the verified decision results. `JUDGE_EVIDENCE.md` maps its claims to the running interface, source, fixtures and limitations. No video is required for the repository submission.

1	"""Deterministic discrete-event model of the Ademix open-pit haulage and crusher system.
     2	
     3	The model is event-driven: trucks move between scheduled events (arrival, end of
     4	loading, end of dumping, bin space available, road cleared). ``step(dt)`` simply
     5	advances the clock to ``now + dt`` and processes every event on the way, so results
     6	do not depend on the publishing tick size. Formulas, units, sources and
     7	limitations are documented in ``MODEL.md``; the what-if scenarios and bottleneck
     8	analysis in ``SCENARIOS.md``.
     9	
    10	Limited resources:
    11	- one excavator that loads one truck at a time (FIFO queue at the face);
    12	- one crusher dump bay that accepts one truck at a time (FIFO queue at the crusher);
    13	- a run-of-mine (ROM) bin of limited capacity that the crusher draws from;
    14	- one two-way haul road with separated direction lanes and a shared speed limit.
    15	"""

    18
